full_prompt:
Draw exactly ONE Small Seal glyph U+3D062.
The supplied chart shows FOUR historical views of the SAME ONE Small Seal character, ordered THX, CCZ, QJZ, DYC. Compare EVERY available witness equally; any slot marked unavailable provides no evidence. Create ONE newly drawn, coherent contemporary sans-serif/Gothic glyph informed by all witnesses, selecting ONE coherent attested construction where variants differ. Never combine incompatible components or replace this with modern Chinese. Trace the real continuous writing-stroke courses using smooth rounded curves and appropriate straight segments; preserve all meaningful branches, legs, bars, counters, crossings, attachments and detachments. Each intentional stroke has the SAME CONSTANT width, approximately 3% of the full canvas, with rounded caps and joins. No brush taper, thick/thin pressure, serifs, texture, ink blobs, doubled outlines or ornamental seal effects. Output exactly ONE complete glyph, black on transparent alpha, centered within the central70% of a square canvas with generous clear margins. No reference copies, four-character layout, labels, text, frames, grid, backdrop or shadows.
STRUCTURAL READING AID:
1. Only THX and QJZ available; CCZ/DYC blank. Left ritual component: short detached top bar, longer lower bar with attached central descender and two detached side descenders.
2. Right upper construction consists of interlocked rounded bends: one center vertical begins with a broad rightward top horizontal, descends through TWO crossing horizontal levels, then curves RIGHT into a short free return well above the inner lower ladder.
3. From that top horizontal a short inner downward hook turns right into a second short free horizontal near the upper-right corner. Preserve this small top-right hook.
4. A separate tall stroke begins upper-left of right construction, descends briefly then turns right across the center vertical into the outer RIGHT descending side. Another tall stroke is the outer LEFT side: it rises to the lower crossing level and curves right into a free horizontal crossing the same center vertical. These two outer sides enclose the lower component but stay open at bottom.
5. Inside the lower enclosure is an upright rounded-top ladder: TWO internal horizontal divisions create EXACTLY THREE stacked counters. Its two sides meet a bottom baseline that extends beyond the ladder to both left and right. Keep visible gaps from ladder to the enclosing side legs, and gap above ladder to the free central return.
Compare the two available witnesses equally and use one coherent attested whole form. Critical details: top-right small hook, interlocked crossing rounded upper bends, two long outside sides, and lower ladder with EXACTLY THREE counters and a broader baseline. Never turn the lower ladder into two or four counters.
